headline: Take-Two gets slammed -4.4% and oil crashes over 5% — a volatile Monday with CGT changes dominating Aussie politics and Google launching Gemini Omni overnight.

portfolio.summary: TTWO was the portfolio's big loser, dropping 4.4% with no clear news catalyst beyond pre-release GTA 6 noise. GOOGL slipped 1.2% despite solid recent earnings. Everything else was relatively flat — the ASX holdings barely moved.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Fell $10.53 to $227.55 USD. No major news; GTA 6 collector's edition pre-order chatter is about all that's circulating. Likely some profit-taking or broader sentiment.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Down $4.69 to $382.97 USD. Broader market drag despite recent strong earnings. Google launched Gemini Omni overnight — watch for any re-rating.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: Soft session in line with WTI crude cratering over 5%. OPEC cut demand growth forecasts for 2026 — headwind for energy holdings.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: Minor dip of $1.55 to $515.51 AUD, broadly tracking the US market.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Small green day, up $0.25 to $92.63 AUD. AUD strength may be a modest tailwind here.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Essentially flat at $418.57 USD. AI and cloud momentum narrative intact per recent coverage.

markets.summary: US markets ended slightly positive — S&P 500 up 0.37%, NASDAQ up 0.19%. ASX 200 slipped 0.41%. The big macro story is WTI crude down 5.28% to $91.50, which is bad for energy holdings but good for inflation. Gold ticked up to $4,542 and the AUD firmed to 0.7173 against the USD.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Gave back ground; mild down day.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Sharp drop — OPEC cut 2026 demand forecast. Headwind for FUEL.AX.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: AUD firm despite fading RBA rate hike bets — see politics section.

politics.summary: Labor is pushing ahead with linking popular income tax cuts to capital gains tax and negative gearing changes — a politically provocative move that's drawing fire. Separately, the RBA rate outlook is in flux, with one outlier expert calling for hikes while markets unwind rate-rise bets and bond demand recovers.

stories.title: Labor ties popular tax cuts to CGT and negative gearing changes
stories.why_it_matters: Labor is bundling income tax cuts with CGT and negative gearing reform — forcing voters and investors to take the package or leave it. If this gets up, it directly affects property investors and anyone holding assets with large capital gains. Watch closely.

stories.title: Labor to ignore call for pause on CGT changes
stories.why_it_matters: Government is pressing ahead despite pushback. No pausing — which signals these changes are serious legislative intent, not a negotiating position.

stories.title: RBA rate rise bets unwind, demand for Australian bonds recovers
stories.why_it_matters: Markets are pricing out RBA hikes, which is pushing bond yields down and bond prices up. Good for rate-sensitive assets, potentially supportive of CBA and property stocks.

stories.title: Why is the AUD rising despite weakening RBA rate hike odds?
stories.why_it_matters: AUD at 0.7173 is worth watching — stronger AUD reduces the value of your USD-denominated holdings (GOOGL, MSFT, TTWO) when converted back to AUD. The decoupling from rate expectations is unusual.

ai.summary: The AI news feed this week is dominated by one story: Pope Leo XIV has released a major papal document calling for robust global AI regulation and flagging autonomous weapons as ungovernable. Meanwhile, Google dropped a big one overnight — introducing Gemini Omni, a new flagship model.

stories.title: Google introduces Gemini Omni
stories.why_it_matters: Brand-new multimodal model from Google, published overnight. This is directly relevant to GOOGL — a meaningful product release that could drive re-rating if Gemini Omni lands well against GPT-4o and Claude. Worth reading the blog post.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV issues sweeping call for AI regulation and ethical oversight
stories.why_it_matters: The Vatican's first formal AI policy document is a signal of where global regulatory sentiment is heading. Pope Leo specifically called out autonomous weapons as beyond human control — adding moral weight to calls for international AI governance frameworks. Not an immediate market mover, but shapes the regulatory backdrop for Big Tech.

sport.summary: NRL is gearing up for Round 13 with some significant injury concerns at the Warriors and Tigers. In the surf, a WSL event in New Zealand was halted after an Aussie photographer was bitten by what's believed to be a shark. AFL had a big weekend, with Brisbane Lions under the microscope and news of Neale Daniher's legacy being celebrated.

stories.title: WSL event in NZ halted after Australian photographer bitten by shark or sea lion
stories.why_it_matters: WSL surf comp paused in NZ after an Aussie photographer was attacked in the water. The event is on hold — no surfing on the Gold Coast angle but relevant for surf fans and the WSL calendar.

stories.title: NRL Round 13 team tips: Warriors and Tigers cop injury blows, Origin stars in doubt
stories.why_it_matters: Warriors and Tigers both dealing with injury blows heading into Round 13. State of Origin selections also creating uncertainty around team lists.

stories.title: Lions slaughter exposed AFL's biggest farce — one last chance to fix it
stories.why_it_matters: Brisbane Lions are drawing scrutiny after a big win exposed what commentators are calling a structural flaw in the AFL competition. Hot topic for AFL fans this week.

stories.title: Fighter, fundraiser, family: Neale Daniher leaves a legacy greater than football
stories.why_it_matters: Touching tribute to Neale Daniher, the former Melbourne coach who has battled MND for over a decade while raising tens of millions for research. A proper read.

watch_today.title: TTWO down 4.4% — monitor for further weakness
watch_today.detail: No single clear catalyst for the drop. If selling continues early in the session, worth deciding whether to hold or trim ahead of GTA 6 launch window. Sharp move deserves attention today.

watch_today.title: Oil down 5.3% — headwind for FUEL.AX
watch_today.detail: WTI crude at $91.50 after OPEC cut 2026 demand growth forecasts. FUEL.AX already slipped 0.68%. If oil keeps sliding, the ETF will follow. Watch the energy sector open today.

watch_today.title: Labor's CGT + tax cuts bundle — portfolio implications
watch_today.detail: If CGT changes pass, assets with embedded capital gains (including shares held long-term) will face higher tax on disposal. Worth reviewing your cost base and whether any rebalancing ahead of potential changes makes sense.

watch_today.title: Google launches Gemini Omni — potential GOOGL catalyst
watch_today.detail: Published overnight. A strong reception could provide a positive re-rating for GOOGL after its 1.2% dip. Read the blog post and watch for analyst commentary today.

watch_today.title: AUD strengthening to 0.7173 — reduces USD holding values
watch_today.detail: Your GOOGL, MSFT, and TTWO holdings are USD-denominated. A stronger AUD quietly erodes returns when converted back. Not urgent but worth tracking if AUD continues to climb.
